name: Acute Megakaryoblastic Leukemia in Children with Down Syndrome
aliases: Acute Megakaryoblastic Leukemia associated with Trisomy 21

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of ≥20% blasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Blasts showing megakaryocytic differentiation confirmed by immunophenotyping (CD41, CD61 positivity)
Diagnosis in a child with Down syndrome or constitutional trisomy 21
Exclusion of other acute leukemia subtypes by morphology and immunophenotyping

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: ≥20% blasts in bone marrow with megakaryocytic immunophenotype in a child with Down syndrome
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for GATA1 mutations supports diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Severe low platelet count leading to petechiae and mucosal bleeding
searchTerms: very low platelets with bleeding risk
bleeding tendency due to low platelets

pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by bone marrow biopsy and immunophenotyping
searchTerms: marrow infiltration by immature platelet cells

common.symptomName: Anemia presenting with pallor and fatigue
searchTerms: fatigue and pale skin due to low red cells

common.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to leukemic infiltration

occasional.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes in some cases
Rarely due to high blast counts
searchTerms: breathing difficulty from blood cell buildup
lung problems due to high white cell count

occasional.notes: Headache, cranial nerve palsies in rare CNS infiltration
searchTerms: nerve problems due to CNS disease

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to leukemic infiltration
Cardiovascular complications from anemia or infection
rare.notes: Rare congestive heart failure or shock
searchTerms: heart and circulation problems from anemia or infection
cardiovascular complications related to low blood counts
heart issues caused by anemia or infection

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing circulating megakaryoblasts
Immunophenotyping positive for CD41, CD61, CD42b
imaging: Chest X-ray to evaluate respiratory complications
MRI brain if CNS involvement suspected
other: Cytogenetic analysis excluding other leukemia subtypes

redFlags: Rapid onset of severe thrombocytopenia with bleeding
Progressive bone marrow failure with pancytopenia
references: Arber DA, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, Revised 4th Edition, 2016.
Hasle H. Acute leukemia in children with Down syndrome. Leukemia. 2001;15(6): 1013-1021.
Roberts I, et al. GATA1 mutations in transient myeloproliferative disorder and acute megakaryoblastic leukemia of Down syndrome. Blood. 2003;102(1): 296-301.
